<reason>Side B wins by demonstrating that capping international recruitment fails to free family-suitable housing (as students occupy shared rooms or purpose-built accommodation that families cannot use), harms domestic students by removing tuition cross-subsidies, and discriminates based on nationality rather than housing need. B's alternative—requiring contracted beds for any enrollment growth—achieves the housing protection goal immediately via master-leasing on the same admissions cycle, neutralizing A's immediacy advantage while avoiding the collateral damage.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 (B4.1–B4.3), where B answers the pressure questions by proposing immediate "conditional admission" via master-leasing existing blocks, showing this operates on the same timeline as a cap but actually removes newcomers from the family rental market, and demonstrating that domestic enrollment growth is equally discretionary.</best_rebuttal>
